Realistic challenges to this outcome would require either stronger-than-expected convective cooling or an unforecast shift in boundary-layer mixing; however, model agreement and the absence of significant dynamic triggers kept those probabilities below 1 %. The market’s near-certain pricing therefore captures both the physical forecast and the resolution criteria tied to official Denver observations.

Lower readings remain improbable given overnight lows near 24–25 °C and the residual warmth of late-summer conditions. Traders are therefore weighting the most recent model runs and real-time cloud trends that will determine whether the thermometer tops out just below or just above the 29 °C threshold before evening.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Chongqing Jiangbei International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 20 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Chongqing Jiangbei International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/chongqing/ZUCK.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Latest meteorological forecasts for Chongqing on August 20 point to a daytime maximum near 32–33°C under typical late-summer subtropical conditions.** High humidity, scattered cloud cover, and moderating winds are limiting peak solar heating in this mountainous, inland location, which aligns with the market’s strong clustering on 32°C (28%) and 33°C (40.5%) outcomes.

Historical climatology supports this positioning: August highs in Chongqing decline from roughly 34°C early in the month toward 31–32°C by late August, with average peaks around 32–33°C and rare excursions above 35°C absent strong high-pressure systems. Recent model consensus and observational trends show no major heatwave or clear-sky intensification that would push readings into the 34–36°C range favored by lower-probability outcomes, while cooler scenarios below 31°C remain unlikely given persistent warm, moist air masses. Traders are therefore weighting the implied probabilities toward the narrow 31–33°C band pending final official station readings.

Historical data show occasional excursions above 32°C when steering patterns weaken the usual afternoon rain shield, aligning with the current market-implied distribution that assigns roughly 70% probability to 32–34°C.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) activity across Luzon is moderating Manila temperatures ahead of August 21, with PAGASA forecasts showing highs of 31–32 °C and 40–70% rain chances under cloudy, humid conditions. These factors suppress peak heating compared with clearer-sky baselines, keeping the daily maximum near the long-term August average of roughly 30–31 °C at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport station. Recent model runs and observational trends favor 31–32 °C resolution, with the tight market split between those two outcomes reflecting uncertainty in exact cloud cover and convective timing. New PAGASA updates tomorrow will provide the final observational anchor for resolution.
